manifest.name: ngm-messaging-manifest
coverage: S2 Messaging ecosystem -> brand_context, framework.ecosystem, framework.evolution
S3 Content -> framework.content_mix, topic_discovery, titles, script_templates, format_adapters

usage.flow: Creator identity > Messaging ecosystem > Topics > Titles > Script template > Format > Test

file_map.brand_context: USER FILLS ONCE — the Messaging Elements Guide
file_map.topic_bank: USER FILLS, GROWS — belief map, misconceptions, objections, winners
file_map.generation_request: PER SCRIPT — what to make right now
file_map.framework: STATIC — principles, patterns, titles, templates, adapters
file_map.output_spec: STATIC — exact shape of the model's answer
file_map.crosswalk: STATIC — NGM <-> market/offer manifest + awareness stages

fill_rules: Leave a field empty (null) rather than guess. Empty fields are skipped.
Write only TRUE specifics (real numbers, real mistakes, real stories). The model uses only what is here and flags gaps as [NEEDS: path.to.field] instead of inventing.
SA / FPH / method names can change anytime. The audience never sees them as labels.
usage.notes_convention: Each top-level part has a _notes object: the YAML inline comments, keyed by path relative to that part (a.b[0].c). Fill guidance, allowed values and examples live there.

_notes.creator.expertise: what you actually do and have done — the ground your mastery stands on
_notes.creator.languages: e.g. [en, sk] — first one is the default script language
_notes.creator.platforms.main: ONE hub: instagram | youtube | podcast | tiktok | linkedin | facebook
_notes.voice: how YOU talk. The creator is the light that attracts the audience.
_notes.voice.tone_words: e.g. direct, warm, playful, calm authority
_notes.voice.energy: e.g. calm teacher | fired-up coach | dry humor
_notes.voice.sample_transcript: 150-300 words of you talking naturally (transcript, not polished copy). Strongest voice signal.
_notes.identity: S1 "Remembering who you are" — content is built from this, not from audience surveys
_notes.identity.core_values: top 5 you want inside the business (they attract people like you)
_notes.identity.identities: top 3 you want visible: parent, entrepreneur, athlete, traveler…
_notes.identity.things_i_want_to_say: what you've held back out of fear of judgment / haters
_notes.identity.silence_notes: raw ideas that came in silence, shower, walks, journaling — unfiltered
_notes.identity.natural_ability: what you "just get" faster than most (zone of genius)
_notes.identity.mastery.lived_experience: things you've actually done, repeatedly (deeper KNOWing) — story fuel
_notes.identity.mastery.failures_and_lessons: feeds Top Mistakes content, stories, proof
_notes.identity.mastery.original_ip: terms / frameworks / methods unique in FUNCTION, not just renamed
_notes.identity.boundaries: Personal Power — hard lines the model must never cross
_notes.identity.boundaries.topics_off_limits: e.g. politics, trending news unrelated to your message
_notes.identity.boundaries.never_do: e.g. name competitors, apologize for a stance, mock the audience
_notes.identity.boundaries.audience_never_gets: emotional boundary, e.g. my anger, my worry — keeps tone secure, not defensive
_notes.struggling_avatar: SA — an identity the audience adopts as their own label AND wants to leave
_notes.struggling_avatar.name: adjective(s) + identity noun, e.g. "Overwhelmed Educator". Softer: positive-negative combo ("Struggling but Optimistic Wanderer")
_notes.struggling_avatar.source: me_earlier (default — an older version of you) | favorite_client (if you never lived it)
_notes.struggling_avatar.struggles_and_emotions: before the transformation, e.g. burnout, lost, working hard, stuck
_notes.struggling_avatar.description: 2-4 sentences in THEIR words — how they think, what they do, how it feels
_notes.future_paced_hero: FPH — the identity they desire; ideally where you are now
_notes.future_paced_hero.name: e.g. "Powerful Founder". Tip: echo the method name ("Powerful Founder" <-> "Powerful Founders Method")
_notes.future_paced_hero.transformation: adjective | noun | both   (lost business owner -> powerful CEO = both)
_notes.future_paced_hero.feelings: how they feel once they have the result
_notes.future_paced_hero.movement_name: optional — a movement you want to create
_notes.unique_solution: the bridge SA -> FPH; the northstar every TR / WTD piece points to
_notes.unique_solution.name: FPH (or theme) + Effect | Method | Process | Solution
_notes.unique_solution.type: element (ingredients that must combine, any order) | framework (ordered steps)
_notes.unique_solution.simple_promise: the main PROBLEM it solves (not what you do)
_notes.unique_solution.passes_10_expert_test: true if 10 other experts asked for a process would NOT give you the same steps
_notes.unique_solution.desire_but: optional — model derives from pillars if empty (3-pillar version)
_notes.unique_solution.drawing_notes: how you draw / explain it on a whiteboard (for visuals)
_notes.deeper_purpose: NOT a result. The effect left on the world when 10,000 people get your result.
_notes.deeper_purpose.change_i_want_to_see: in the world / nation / town / industry
_notes.deeper_purpose.stage_moment: you crushed it on stage, people said it changed their life — what did you talk about?
_notes.deeper_purpose.top_results: helper: your 3 strongest client results and how their lives (and people around them) change
_notes.diagnosis: be the one who "discovers the illness" — whoever names it is who they go to for the cure
_notes.diagnosis.symptoms: specific pain, e.g. "posting 4+ times a week, content is good, still blending in"
_notes.diagnosis.causes: what they specifically do that creates it, e.g. "70%+ of posts are tutorials"
_notes.diagnosis.advice_causing_it: popular advice that keeps the problem alive
_notes.diagnosis.common_enemy.name: your name for the problem — you and the audience rally against it
_notes.specific_library: fuel for every pattern. REAL, accurately specific: numbers, time frames, frequencies, measurements
_notes.specific_library.feelings: say the feeling without naming it, e.g. "refresh views every 20 minutes after posting"
_notes.specific_library.mistakes[0].they_know_i: false = hidden cause (strongest material: they never linked THIS to THAT)
_notes.specific_library.pains: extra pains not tied to a single mistake
_notes.specific_library.desires: specific things they want / things you now have
_notes.specific_library.time_based_identifiers: ready lines — "if you've been {pain} for more than {time}…"
_notes.proof_bank: the ONLY evidence the model may cite
_notes.proof_bank.counter_examples: well-known 3rd parties the audience recognizes; must be DOING your solution
_notes.proof_bank.counter_examples[0]: person, company, book, film, historical moment
_notes.proof_bank.stories: your own — origin, turning points, client wins, failures
_notes.offers_and_ctas.lead_magnet: free training, webinar, video series, guide, challenge
_notes.offers_and_ctas.lead_magnet.how_to_get: link in bio | comment KEYWORD | DM | URL
_notes.offers_and_ctas.core_offer.not_covered_i: what free content deliberately leaves out
_notes.offers_and_ctas.core_offer.problems_when: problems that appear without those parts -> one_and_more, new bigger promise

_notes.belief_map: Exercise 1 — work backwards: specific problem -> action -> belief behind it
_notes.belief_map[0]: e.g. "flat audience and sales for 3+ months"
_notes.belief_map[0].action: what they do (or don't do) that causes it
_notes.belief_map[0].belief: the belief / norm that drives the action
_notes.belief_map[0].core_belief: the root, stripped down (used by context_switch), e.g. "information = results"
_notes.belief_map[0].causes_suffering_70: true if it hurts 70%+ of people who hold it
_notes.belief_map[0].works_for_30: true if it genuinely works for 30%+ -> pet peeve, don't reverse it
_notes.per_scope: Exercise 2 — once for the whole unique solution, then once per pillar
_notes.per_scope[0].misconceptions: what the outside world gets wrong
_notes.per_scope[0].outdated_norms: "the way it's done" that is now bad / old
_notes.per_scope[0].limiting_beliefs: the SA's own limiting beliefs about this
_notes.per_scope[0].framework: the process, if there is one
_notes.per_scope[0].beliefs_to_stand_up_for: beliefs about the SA they'd LOVE you to defend
_notes.per_scope[0].shared_beliefs: you + SA + FPH all believe these
_notes.topics.connection.traditional: beliefs the SA shares that relate to your work
_notes.topics.connection.identity: 3-4 personal themes (behind the scenes, family, training, travel…)
_notes.performance_log: S4 — what worked. Winners become campaign angles and title retests.
_notes.performance_log[0].signals: avg watch time, saves, shares, comments, ThruPlay cost

_notes.template: e.g. thought_reversal.og — empty = model picks via framework.routing and says why
_notes.target_belief: TR: the ONE belief to reverse
_notes.pillar: which unique_solution pillar this serves (TR / WTD)
_notes.format: reel_short | video_long | live | image_post | slider | podcast_episode | email | ad | webinar_segment | video_series_segment | sales_video | caption_only
_notes.language: overrides creator.languages[0]; "bilingual" = spoken in one, caption in both
_notes.title_style: see framework.titles — empty = mix styles across variants
_notes.aggression: auto | low | medium | high   (auto = from niche_state)
_notes.audience_awareness: optional: unaware | problem_aware | solution_aware | product_aware | most_aware
_notes.variants: title / hook variants to test "how to say it"
_notes.source_transcript: repurpose / documentation mode: paste the staple piece or talk

llm_procedure.role: You are a scriptwriter trained in the New Generation Mastery messaging framework. You write in the creator's own voice, from their identity and stance, to move viewers from unaware to aware and create demand for the creator's unique solution.
steps: Read generation_request and resolve mode, content_type, template (framework.routing if empty), format adapter, length, language
Pull the relevant ecosystem elements (SA, FPH, unique solution or pillar, common enemy, deeper purpose)
Pull real specifics from specific_library and proof from proof_bank that fit this topic (2+ for short form, 4+ for long form)
For sales pieces, check topic_bank.performance_log and reuse winning titles, angles and language
Write title variants with framework.titles for the content type
Draft section by section following the template steps, embedding the named language patterns
Adapt to the format (length, on-screen text, caption, slides)
Run quality_checklist, fix what fails, and list anything missing in needs
Return exactly the output_spec shape and nothing else
audience_facing_language: Never put internal terms in spoken text or captions (struggling avatar, future paced hero, thought reversal, SOM, CTA, pillar, ecosystem) unless the creator's audience uses them
SA and FPH NAMES are used naturally as identities ("most {SA name}s do X"); the method name and common enemy name are used as proper nouns
Write for the ear — short sentences, contractions, rhythm, the creator's own phrases
Never label steps out loud ("step 3, the discredit…")

principles.speak_to_the_subconscious: Aim for automatic reactions ("that's me", "never thought of it like that", "that makes so much sense") instead of a logical debate. Pure information makes the viewer evaluate; great content makes them feel. Encyclopedias are full of information and never top the bestseller lists.

stop_the_automation.idea: People run on beliefs their subconscious automated without critical thought. Each piece interrupts ONE automation, moves the viewer from unaware to aware, and hands them a better belief. More steps and tutorials usually reinforce the old automation instead.

explaining_looks_like: citing stats as the selling point
here's why you need my solution
persuading_looks_like: showing the belief's flaw from an angle they never saw
undeniable proof or a counter example
showing the other options are flawed instead of praising yours

principles.beliefs_not_opinions: Target what people hold as TRUTH without having questioned it. Never argue an opinion to be right. The creator's opinion never needs to appear — the belief's flaw does the work.
principles.accurate_specificity: Vague lets the subconscious escape ("not relevant to me"). Specific doesn't. Use numbers, time frames, frequencies, measurements and real behaviors from the specific library, chosen so they are true for most of the audience. Say "overwhelmed" without saying overwhelmed.
principles.compassion_and_personal_power: Secure, never defensive. Show the flaws of OLD METHODS that cause suffering — never call out, cancel, mock or complain about people. Acknowledge why someone holds a belief before discrediting it. Aim every discredit at the belief, never at the viewer's worth.
personal_power_red_flags: posts about what other people do (unless praising and sharing their work)
calling people out or canceling them
riding media trends unrelated to the creator's message and impact
choosing what to say based on how people might react
apologizing for a stance that doesn't need an apology
messages that won't be true in 5 years
principles.creator_is_the_light: The creator's identities, values and beliefs attract the audience. Write from their stance; don't water it down to please everyone. Repelling people who don't share the values is a feature.
principles.teach_what_not_how: Free content teaches WHAT to do and why. The full HOW lives in the offer. Teaching everything overwhelms people or convinces them they already have all they need.
principles.northstar_consistency: Every Thought Reversal and What-To-Do piece connects to the unique solution or one of its pillars. No random topics. Connection content ties to the deeper purpose, core values or identities.
three_jobs_of_content: create demand (remove a belief -> desire for the new way)
principles.ecosystem_not_single_piece: Messaging is experienced over many pieces. One script does one job well and doesn't need to carry the whole message.
principles.evolution_70_percent: 70% perfect is perfect. Every script is a test of WHAT to say and HOW to say it, so always offer title and hook variants.
principles.no_fabrication: The workbook's specifics land because they are real. Use only specifics, stories, stats and results from brand_context and topic_bank. Counter examples must be real and widely known. If something is missing, write [NEEDS: field.path] — never invent it.

ecosystem.model: A house on a street full of houses. The title is the blue door that gets someone inside. Once inside, every element across many pieces makes them FEEL whether this is the right house.

elements.struggling_avatar: Identity the audience self-labels as and does NOT want to stay. Built from an older version of the creator.
elements.future_paced_hero: Identity they desire. Comes out the other side of the unique solution.
elements.unique_solution: The creator's own method (3-5 pillars) that bridges SA to FPH. Separates them from "an expert in a sea of experts".
elements.deeper_purpose: The why behind the work — the effect on the world, not the client result. Powers connection.
elements.diagnosis_and_common_enemy: The named cause of their pain. Naming it makes the creator the one to fix it and unites the audience against it.
elements.specific_library: Real feelings, mistakes, pains, desires. What makes the subconscious say "that's me".
elements.thought_reversal_content: Shifts perspective by ending a belief that causes suffering. Builds thought leadership and brings people in.
elements.connection_content: Builds know-like-trust by rallying around shared beliefs, values and identities.
elements.what_to_do_content: Educates from mastery, always tied to the unique solution.
elements.titles: The blue door. Stop the scroll, then the ecosystem does the rest.

usage_rules: When listing a mistake, problem, myth or consequence, tie it to the SA identity so viewers adopt the label
Present the FPH as the destination identity ("this is what {FPH name}s do")
Name the unique solution when it bridges the gap; name the common enemy when describing the cause
Use labels naturally — a label in every sentence reads as a gimmick

1.name: Unheard
1.symptom: helpful content nobody watches; flat for 3+ months
1.cause: 70%+ information / tutorial content, generalized, topics chosen by what the audience says it wants

2.name: Seen
2.symptom: titles get attention, but viewers don't stay, engage or convert
2.cause: titles improved, scripts don't hold attention or create the head-nod

3.name: Heard
3.symptom: engagement and DMs, but sales inconsistent
3.cause: focused on being different rather than creating demand; no own IP or named solution yet

4.name: Hustle-selling
4.symptom: fairly consistent but unscalable sales via big efforts and small launches; cold traffic doesn't convert
4.cause: still too much teaching; not specific enough that people FEEL the creator solves their suffering

5.name: Scalable
5.symptom: predictable growth, cold traffic converts, people ask how to work together before the pitch
5.cause: deep specificity and action — but still educating an existing industry

6.name: New Generation Mastery
6.symptom: people cite the creator's "work", others teach it, "you changed my life" is common
6.cause: full alignment and critical thinking; creating a new way instead of regurgitating

content_mix.experimental_story_note: Vlogs, behind the scenes, entertainment — test freely. Story pieces still belong to one of the three types.

som.purpose: Discredit a belief so it can't be argued with. The core of every TR discredit and every objection.
som.follow_up_enhancer: Can you find me any {successful_example_group} that didn't {do_the_solution}?

chunk_up.move: Apply the belief to everyone, 100% of the time, and let it collapse.
chunk_up.template: If {belief} were true, everyone who {does_it} would {get_result}, right? We know that isn't the case.

chunk_down.move: Point to one specific time the belief wasn't true.
chunk_down.template: Has there ever been a time you {did_the_belief} and still didn't {get_result}?

metaphor_analogy.move: Show the flaw through a comparison.

counter_example.move: A well-known third-party example where the belief fails AND the solution is being used. Not your own testimonial. Avoid stats.

hierarchy_of_criteria.move: Move their focus to something more important.
hierarchy_of_criteria.template: Isn't it more important to focus on {higher_value} than on {belief_focus}?

change_frame_size.move: Enlarge or shrink the frame until the belief looks insignificant, or ask them to define it.
change_frame_size.template: How much {belief_measure} counts as enough? If {big_outcome} happened, would {belief} still matter?

meta_frame.move: Challenge where the belief came from.
meta_frame.template: Is that really yours, or something you heard from {source} so many times it started to feel true?
meta_frame.caution: The workbook's harsher versions question the person's character. In public content, question the belief's source — never shame the viewer.

consequence.move: Shift attention to where the belief leads. Also reinforces beliefs you want kept.
consequence.template: What happens if you hold on to {belief} for another {timeframe}? {real_consequence}.

intention.move: Acknowledge the positive intent, then show the flaw.
intention.template: I know the intention is {positive_intent}, but doesn't {belief} end up {negative_effect}?

another_outcome.move: Reveal it's really about something else, which makes letting go easier.
another_outcome.template: Is this really about {surface_topic}, or about {real_issue}?

reality_strategy.move: Ask how, specifically, the belief is true and where it comes from.
reality_strategy.template: How specifically does {belief} lead to {result}? Which {part} exactly?

model_of_the_world.move: Present another widely held perspective that pulls them off theirs.
model_of_the_world.template: Did you know most {successful_group} say {different_view} is what actually made the difference?

desire_but.purpose: Explain the unique solution AND create demand for it — shows why every pillar is needed and which pillar fixes their current pain.
desire_but.logic: For each pair of pillars, state the desire they produce together, BUT the pain that remains because the third is missing. Then all together gives the result they want most.
desire_but.template: When you have {p1} and {p2} you get {p1_p2_result}, but without {p3} you'll still face {p3_missing_pain}. With {p2} and {p3} you get {p2_p3_result}, but without {p1} you'll {p1_missing_pain}. With {p1} and {p3} you get {p1_p3_result}, but without {p2} you'll {p2_missing_pain}. Put all of them together and you get {all_combined_result}. They only work together, which is why you've probably been feeling {current_pain}.

list_method.purpose: Make them feel automatically that you understand the problem, why it exists, and can fix it — without saying you have the solution.

variants.pain_to_cause: If you're {specific_pain_1}, {specific_pain_2}, or {specific_pain_3}… then I guarantee you're doing at least one of these: {specific_action_1}, {specific_action_2}, {specific_action_3}. Am I right?
variants.cause_to_pain: If you're doing even one of these — {specific_action_1}, {specific_action_2}, {specific_action_3} — then I guarantee you're {specific_pain}. Am I right?

one_and_more.purpose: Teach one thing while telling the subconscious there's more in the offer or next step. Makes them WANT the teaching before it starts.
steps: Promise — I'm about to show you {promise}.
Specific mistakes — Most people {specific_mistakes}.
Specific pain — And because of that {specific_pain}.
Sell without selling — There are {n} ways / steps to this inside {offer_or_next_step}…
Remove the selling (optional in content, use in sales mechanisms) — …but I'm giving you my favorite one right now because {reason}, and with it you'll {result} {by_when}.

time_based_identifier.purpose: Get accurately specific fast so the right person self-identifies.
time_based_identifier.template: If you've been {specific_pain} for more than {time}, then you're {specific_action_or_non_action}.
time_based_identifier.tip: Pick one problem and a timeframe that is true for most of the audience.

roa_method.purpose: Position the creator's solution as the only viable option by discrediting the alternatives.
steps: Desired results + mistakes — paint the result they want, then the mistakes stopping it
Options — list the options they're considering (including yours); discredit each alternative with a question it can't survive; yours remains
Objections as actions — voice what people think or do when trying your option (fear, gear, doubt) and remove it with SOM (chunk up, counter example)
CTA — how to get your solution and do it right

context_switch.purpose: Put the belief into a context where it's obviously false. The automation stops and they think critically ("never thought of it like that").
steps: Core belief — reduce the belief to its root (e.g. "how-to content builds an audience" -> "information = results")
Contexts — find 2-3 situations where that root belief is clearly not true
No-questions — ask each as a question whose answer is "no"
Bridge — "So why do you do the same thing in your {business/life}?" + name exactly how they're doing it

self_identifying.purpose: Specific problems + specific cause + a label, so they categorize themselves and assume you hold the fix.

structures.label_last: {specific problems} + {specific cause} -> if that's you, you're {label}
structures.label_first: You're probably dealing with {label} if {specific problems} — and it usually means {specific cause}.

self_identifying.requirement: Accurately specific behaviors, causes and emotions. The specificity triggers "that's me".

explaining_the_unexplained.purpose: Give words to a pain they live with but can't explain. The realization itself is the value.
steps: find a pain they haven't solved
explain what causes it
combine into one statement
explaining_the_unexplained.template: {pain they deal with} happens when {cause}, because {mechanism}.

diagnosis_reveal.purpose: Like the first doctor to identify an unknown illness — describe the symptoms and causes so accurately, then NAME it, that the creator becomes the obvious one to fix it. The name becomes a common enemy the creator and audience rally against.
steps: specific symptoms
specific actions causing them
the popular advice keeping it alive
name it (common enemy)
signal that it's fixable

rules: Choose aggression by what the NICHE responds to, not the creator's comfort
One belief per TR title; beliefs, not opinions
Always return variants so WHAT to say and HOW to say it can be tested
Mix title styles across pieces

thought_reversal.question: Is {belief} really the best way to {desired_result}?

connection.should_need: {identity or core value} {should | do | need to | always} {belief}
connection.create_make: {identity or core value} {create | make} {what you create or want to create}
connection.note: Identity connection posts usually need no title — image + caption.

what_to_do.without: How to {result} without {common mistake or disliked task}

ad_headlines: a TR title (only when the creative has no title bar)

topic_discovery.belief_chain: Beliefs create actions, actions create results. Start from specific problems and work backwards to action, then belief.

pet_peeve_filter.keep_if: the belief causes suffering for 70%+ of the people who hold it
pet_peeve_filter.drop_if: the belief genuinely works for 30%+ of people (a pet peeve, not a reversal)

topic_discovery.thought_reversal_topics: Up to 5 of the most relatable beliefs from belief_map, then fill to 10 from misconceptions, outdated norms, limiting beliefs, objections (listening and buying) and the most backwards thing.
topic_discovery.what_to_do_topics: Up to 5 as "how to fix {problem}" from belief_map problems, then fill to 10 from elements/steps and framework. Pick what MOST people need, not favorites.
topic_discovery.connection_topics: Deeper purpose + beliefs the SA shares that aren't about the offer + 3-4 identity themes.
topic_discovery.self_identifying_education_topics: Take how-to or TR topics that exist because of a misconception. Ask "why?" and "where else does this happen?" to find more misconceptions, then title for curiosity.

thought_reversal.context_switch_when: the core belief has an obvious everyday parallel where it's clearly false — great for short form
thought_reversal.self_identify_when: requested, or messaging_level is 3+ (advanced — OG and context switch come first)
thought_reversal.podcast_tr_when: format is podcast_episode or a live longer than 15 min

what_to_do.persuasive_tutorial_when: the topic has real steps (pillar or framework)
what_to_do.statement_and_example_when: a strong story or case exists in proof_bank
what_to_do.top_mistakes_when: failures_and_lessons has material on the topic
what_to_do.breakdown_review_when: a showable example with clout exists
what_to_do.self_identifying_education_when: the topic exists because of a misconception; format is slider or caption

connection.format_4_passion_write_when: the creator supplies a raw letter

thought_reversal.intent: End suffering by reversing ONE belief or norm that causes the problem, then move them to the better way. Most TRs turn educational in the second half — they still count as TR because the intent is the perspective shift.
dos: Keep topics tied to the business or the change the creator wants in the world
Persuade — show how the old way is flawed rather than proving you're right
Use ACTUAL beliefs, not pet peeves
Always move them to the better way after the discredit
donts: Don't state an opinion and move on
Don't explain, especially at the start — if you're justifying why your way is right, you've lost
Don't aim to prove someone wrong; aim to end suffering and cause good change

steps.do: Open against the belief — wrong, bad, outdated, or the old way to get {desired_result}. Usually mirrors the title.
They'll want to defend it. Show you understand why they believe it and where it came from (authority, repetition, "always done this way").
The most important step. Use SOM so it can't be argued. A counter example must be DOING the solution. Default to counter_example or chunk_up.
What keeps happening if they hold on to the belief — specific and real.
They now want the new way. Deliver it as a short What-To-Do (what, not the full how).
Instead of teaching, use hierarchy_of_criteria and questions to lift them off the old perspective.
Keep {old belief} and {pain}, or move to {new way} and {benefit}?
Where to go next.
Reduce the belief to its root (internal prep — not spoken).
2-3 questions from contexts where the root belief is clearly false, each answered with "no".
Ask "so why do you do the same thing in your {business/life}?" + name exactly how they're doing it.
Same as og step 4.
Same as og step 5a.
Same as og step 6.
Same as og step 7.
Open with "there are {3-5} things almost every {identity} does that {bigger problem}…" then list them with precise specifics. Brainstorm 10, keep the 3-5 the solution fixes.
3-6 sentences max, stated as facts, on why those mistakes cause the problem. Longer means over-explaining.
1-2 examples (people, books, companies, films) that don't make these mistakes and DO use the solution — proof for step 2. Steps 2 and 3 may swap.
Same as og step 5a.
Same as og step 6.
Same as og step 7.
What they're about to learn and the pain it fixes — or state that their beliefs are wrong / the old way.
In detail, and why it exists.
Name the common beliefs and industry norms behind the pain and reverse them to create demand.
Stories, several SOM patterns, counter examples, personal stories.
About halfway through.
After each step run 7 and 8.
Stories, examples, metaphors — several.
What goes wrong without this step.
Summarize, restate the problems, CTA to the solution.

connection.intent: Build rapport and a movement. Instead of shifting a perspective, rally around a belief both sides already hold, so they automatically feel "I like this person" — or realize they don't, which is also useful.

subtypes.deeper_purpose: The why behind the brand — purpose, not results.
subtypes.traditional: Beliefs tied to what the creator does or teaches that the audience shares.
subtypes.identity: Personal or behind-the-scenes posts that reinforce an identity (usually image + caption).

dos: Speak from the heart — energy beats a perfect template
Topics the creator will still be fired up about in 5 years
Weave identities and core values in where they fit, never forced
donts: Don't chase media or niche trends, or topics others say you should cover
No politics unless the brand is about politics
No whining, complaining or standing on top of others — stand FOR something
format_1_rally: 1 · Connect — state the belief you stand for
2 · Separate — what MOST people do that's the opposite (something THIS audience isn't doing) -> shared common enemy
3 · Future pace — how this belief becomes the norm
4 · Proof — examples of it already becoming the norm (counter examples)
5 · Solution / consequence — the change needed; optionally the real consequence if it doesn't happen
6 · Rally up — it's OUR job / mission to stand up for it
7 · Choose — a powerful question about where and who they want to be
format_2_stand_for: 1 · State what you stand for in the fewest words (never say 'this is what I stand for')
2 · Describe it and its effect in 2-4 sentences — powerful over long
3 · Effect — on the world, society, community, niche or a type of person
4 · Blame ONE common enemy for why it isn't the norm yet
5 · What if — paint the future if that enemy disappeared
6 · Rally — that future is what you stand for and will build with them

format_3_interview.mode: The creator answers on camera, audio or in writing; an editor or the model assembles the answers in this order. The model can either tailor the questions to a belief or assemble supplied answers.
questions: What does it mean to you?
Why is it important — what problems made it important?
How do we live it or fix that problem?
Who has already lived it, and what did they do or experience?

format_4_passion_write.mode: The creator free-writes a letter to the world about the change they want and why the work matters. Model role is a light edit only (or rearranging into format 1 or 2) — keep the creator's words.

what_to_do.intent: Educate from mastery on the unique solution, engagingly. Never plain tutorials only — mix these types.
dos: Actually educate — persuasion must not crowd out the teaching
Move away from regurgitated teachings; use the creator's own language and what others don't teach
Build demand and engagement while teaching
After points, add stories, examples, mistakes, pain points, metaphors and multiple scenarios so viewers apply it to themselves
donts: Don't teach the full HOW (that's the offer)
No more than ~10 min of pure information without stories, examples or metaphors

uses: top of funnel short and long
structure: Intro to the whole piece — one_and_more (promise, mistakes, pain, there are {n} steps / ways)
For EACH step — intro (short one_and_more: promise, mistakes, pain, sell without selling) -> teach -> outro
Outro — a metaphor, counter example, story, personal or relatable example of the step in action, so they think 'I get it now'
CTA — Now you know how to {promise}, but the problem is {what remains with only this info}, and that's why we created {next step}.
persuasive_tutorial.outline_mode: Unless a full script is requested, outline per step (promise, mistakes, pain, teaching points, examples) so the creator can speak naturally.
persuasive_tutorial.ratio_hint: Most of the script builds demand and pulls people in; only a small share is the actual teaching.

breakdown_review.purpose: Show mastery and borrow social proof by dissecting something with clout (person, brand, book, speech, historical moment) that demonstrates what the creator teaches.
steps: State who or what you're breaking down
The specific mistakes and pain this will end for them
Show, read or play the first part
Break down what they did, contrasted with the mistakes people usually make
Repeat for each part
CTA to learn to do the same
breakdown_review.needs: a real, showable example (link, clip, quote) — flag if missing

documentation.purpose: Clip talks, podcasts, masterminds and events into standalone pieces.
documentation.model_task: From source_transcript, pick self-contained segments that already follow an NGM structure; write title bar, caption and cut points.

statement_and_example.best_in: audio or video, short or long
steps: A statement they haven't realized or don't know how to do (what they'll learn — no steps)
One or more stories, examples or case studies that demonstrate it and teach through it
CTA
State what they're about to get (the top {n} mistakes I made {doing X})
Each mistake — what it was + why you did it (what you thought you'd gain)
The lesson learned from it
Repeat, then CTA
top_mistakes.pairs_with: a separate piece teaching how to do it right

self_identifying_education.purpose: Explain a problem they have but can't explain (or explain wrongly) so precisely that they categorize themselves. Unaware to aware. Do NOT teach the fix.
required: The specific problem each one creates — written as MISTAKE -> PROBLEM pairs, not all mistakes then all problems
A short explanation of why it happens (only if needed — don't over-explain)
CTA to something that helps fix it
self_identifying_education.best_in: sliders (one pair per slide), captions, video

sa_fph_definition.purpose: Define the SA or FPH so viewers self-identify with one and desire the other. Pack in specific pains, mistakes and desires.

comparison_chart.purpose: Two columns — SA vs FPH, old way vs new way (from a winning TR), or two options.

small_tangible_promise.rule: One small, tangible promise per funnel, webinar or series, built from best-performing content. It lets you go deep on specifics while leaving the full solution to be desired.
small_tangible_promise.tangible_means: a clear deliverable, a clear result, or both — ideally with a timeframe
ladder: vague — I'll help you fix your {topic}
tangible + result — Learn our {deliverable} that could {result} within {timeframe}
small_tangible_promise.fit_into_bigger_picture: List what the offer covers that this piece won't, plus the problems when those parts are missing. Weave them in with one_and_more, especially near the end.

new_bigger_promise_transition: The specific benefit they'll get from it
Introduce a new, bigger problem that will now show up
State a new promise that fixes that problem
Move into the offer and pitch

webinar_or_video_series.title: titles.sales_mechanism.webinar_or_series (or the best TR title as-is)
webinar_or_video_series.opening: A big, bold thought reversal (self_identify works well) — or several stacked reversals of the biggest industry norms, naming the solution without teaching it and promising to fix it in the session.
teaching_block: What people normally do and why it's wrong, outdated or leads to problems
Live in compassion (why it makes sense that they do it)
The specific problems they experience (time-based if possible)
The solution you're about to teach
SOM discredit, or show the solution in action (counter example, example)
webinar_or_video_series.connection_placement: Use connection pieces that serve the mechanism's promise (why this matters to the creator, the change it creates) a few times throughout.

objections.when: after the offer during the pitch, or woven into the training before it
objections.which: only common objections — especially time and "can I do this" — never plant financial objections

sales_video_assembly.note: The workbook covers webinars, video series, ads and emails; this sequence reuses their parts.
sequence: Self-identify open — list_method or time_based_identifier on the core pain (SA identity)
Diagnosis — diagnosis_reveal names the common enemy
Thought reversal of the biggest norm keeping them stuck (og or context_switch)
Options — roa_method discredits the alternatives they're weighing
Unique solution — desire_but shows why every pillar is needed
Proof — counter examples, stories and case studies from proof_bank
Offer — new bigger promise + what they get
Objections — time and ability objections via SOM
Choose — stay the SA with {pain} or become the FPH with {benefit}

email.full_tr: The whole email is one TR script leading to the CTA. Subject is the TR title or a webinar-style title (optional [FREE WEBINAR] prefix).
email.tr_within: A regular email that uses a TR to shift one belief along the way.

ad.creative: TR video (test with and without title bars), TR image, or a regular creative
ad.headline: A TR title when the creative has no bars; otherwise the webinar-style "[NEW {MECHANISM}] {benefit} without {current approach}"
ad.copy: Any TR script (og, context_switch or self_identify)
ad.testing: Run as a ThruPlay campaign first, then as opt-in ads with the winner

rules: On-screen hook or title in the first second. TR layout — title bar on top, speaker 16:9 in the middle, captions or the solution line at the bottom
One belief, one idea
Compress — compassion is one line, optional steps are skipped, ONE SOM move in the discredit (or one context-switch pair)
The solution is one "what to do" line or 1-3 quick points
Choose and CTA can merge into one line
Full templates; several SOM moves in the discredit are fine
Stories, examples or metaphors after every point
Never 10+ min of pure information
YouTube — use the platform title field for the TR title instead of on-screen bars

steps: Announce the topic and the benefit
The mistakes people make going after that benefit
The pain those mistakes cause
Present the solution
Go deeper into the solution
Connect — why this means so much to you (deeper purpose)
After each taught step, re-orient newcomers (what they'll learn, the mistakes and pain, the solution, what's covered, what's next and why it matters to you)
Teach the next step; repeat the re-orientation until done
notes: Warm up ~2 min before the discredit so people can join
Up to ~15 min follow a video template, slower and with extra examples; longer follow podcast_tr
TR and WTD topics work best, with connection elements woven in

rules: Text on the image is the title, quote or statement; the caption carries the full script
The caption follows the same template steps as a video

styles.post_it: handwritten note — great for testing TR and connection headlines
styles.quote: a one-sentence perspective shift (TR) or a statement they'll agree with (connection)
styles.graphic: shows the message visually, words optional
styles.meme: pokes fun at the OLD way from a winning TR
styles.comparison_chart: SA vs FPH, old way vs new way
styles.phone_function: mimics a reminder, text or alarm for recurring themes

rules: Slide 1 is the title or hook; one idea (or one mistake -> problem pair) per slide; last slide is the CTA
Best for WTD, TR, and self-identifying labels or categories
The caption can carry the explanation when slides stay short

options: Whole episode as one TR — any TR template, each step stretched; stack SOM moves, stories and counter examples in the discredit
A theme with 2-3 TRs inside — ask where the audience is and which beliefs must be unwound, then write a TR per belief
TR + WTD + connection mixed in one episode

repurposing: Staple piece (podcast / long video) -> clips for reels -> quotes and concepts as image posts
Same image post and caption on IG, FB and LinkedIn
Videos over 2 min also go to YouTube

distribution_and_testing.platform: One main hub (mastery through focus), repurposed to secondary platforms.

posting_strategies.single: Start here — staple pieces posted 1-7x per week, no repurposing.
posting_strategies.staple: One staple piece per week on the hub + daily cut-downs (clips, quotes, graphics) on secondary platforms.
posting_strategies.multiple_staples: Two staple pieces per week + daily cut-downs (needs a team).

test_loop: post (don't rewrite forever — write, record, post)
run video as ThruPlay campaigns (15-second view, roughly $0.01-0.05 each, cold traffic)
what_to_test: WHAT to say — the topic or belief
HOW to say it — title, angle, format

analyze.organic: High-effort signals first (saves, shares, comments), then longest view time.
analyze.thruplay: Average watch time first; break ties with engagement.

adjust.winner: Retest with new titles and angles; make more on the topic in other formats.
adjust.liked_but_flopped: Repost with a new title or angle.

campaign_building: Take the best-performing TR or WTD topic (not connection)
Turn it into the webinar / presentation title (How to {benefit} without {belief}) and the ad headlines; reuse the winning copy
Optional — test 3 title bars on one video; the winner becomes the webinar title
Build the presentation from language that already worked (specifics, counter examples, metaphors) — don't guess

all: Voice matches brand_context.voice — would the creator say this out loud?
Enough real specifics from the specific library (2+ short form, 4+ long form)
Speaks to the subconscious; no long stretch of pure information without a story, example or metaphor
Persuades rather than explains; beliefs, not opinions; nobody is called out
Nothing fabricated; every gap is listed in needs
Ties to the unique solution (TR / WTD) or to the deeper purpose, values or identities (connection)
Teaches WHAT and leaves the full HOW for the offer
Fits the length and format constraints
No internal jargon in audience-facing text
thought_reversal: The discredit uses a named SOM move and can't reasonably be argued
Any counter example actually does the solution
The choose step contrasts pain with benefit
The belief passed the pet-peeve filter
connection: The separate step contrasts with what OTHERS do, not what this audience does
Rally language (we, our job, our mission)
Timeless — still true in 5 years; no trends or politics unless that's the creator's message
what_to_do: Every taught step has an intro and an outro (persuasive tutorial)
Examples or metaphors after each point

sections.spoken: Studying grammar first is the slowest way to actually speak a language.
I get why you do it. School taught it that way, and every textbook opens with verb tables.
But think about your first language. You were speaking in full sentences years before anyone explained a single grammar rule.
Stay in textbook mode and you can hit a 300-day app streak and still freeze the moment a waiter asks you something.
Flip it. Speak from week one — badly, out loud, every day — and let grammar clean up what you're already saying.
So — another year of verb tables, or actually talking by summer?
Comment SPEAK and I'll send you the ten-minute daily routine.

_notes.principles: distilled from S1 + rules repeated across the workbook. Apply to EVERY output.
_notes.principles.stop_the_automation.how_belie: heard from many people -> accepted as true
a method that once worked, now outdated, still followed
_notes.principles.personal_power_red_flags: never produce content that does these
_notes.evolution.messaging_levels: where the creator is -> what the scripts should emphasize
_notes.content_mix: across ALL content — images, videos and podcasts count together
_notes.content_mix.ready_for_change_niche.thoug: can rise once it works, never above 40
_notes.content_mix.thought_reversal_formats: rotate so reversals don't all sound alike
_notes.content_mix.thought_reversal_formats.sel: only after OG and context switch are comfortable
_notes.content_mix.video_share: roughly half video, half other formats
_notes.language_patterns: S2 M3 — tools embedded INSIDE any template. Master 1-2, then add more.
_notes.language_patterns.som: Sleight of Mouth (Robert Dilts) — no belief is true 100% of the time, so any belief can be discredited
_notes.titles.connection: a belief statement + identities / core values / SA / FPH
_notes.sales_mechanisms: S3 M3 V8 + S4 M2 — TR / connection / WTD used inside things that sell
_notes.sales_mechanisms.webinar_or_video_series: wrap EVERY taught step like this — never just teach
_notes.sales_mechanisms.sales_video_assembly: NOT a workbook template — NGM parts stitched for a pre-recorded sales video
_notes.quality_checklist: the model self-checks every script before returning it
_notes.example: structure illustration ONLY — mirror the structure, never borrow the content

rules: spoken text is written to be said out loud, in the requested language
sections map 1:1 to template steps, in order, so they can become timeline beats
fields that don't apply to the format are omitted

_notes.return_format: one JSON object with the keys below, nothing else
_notes.script.meta.template_reason: one line, only when the model chose the template
_notes.script.titles[0].style: aggressive | statement | gentle | question | how_to | without | fixing | should_need | create_make | …
_notes.script.sections[0].pattern: language pattern used here, if any
_notes.script.sections[0].visual_note: talking head, b-roll, graphic, screen recording, prop
_notes.script.sections[0].broll_query: search phrase for the footage library (optional)
